shipped_rows.title_o: Studies of independence and conformity: I. A minority of one against a unanimous majority.

blind_target.authors: Uchida, Akitoshi; Michael, Robert B.; Mori, Kazuo
blind_target.title: Scholastic achievement levels and conformity of junior high school students in the Asch experiment
blind_target.evidence_quote: Summarizing, we expect to find a positive association between social approval and conformity (H 4 ), and negative associations for intelligence (H 5 ) and self-esteem (H 6 ).
blind_target.outcome_quote: Finally, we measured the Big Five, intelligence, self-esteem and social approval. With the exception of openness, our study finds no support that these personality traits are statistically significantly related to the susceptibility of group pressure.
blind_target.outcome_reasoning: Original higher achievement predicted lower conformity; current intelligence association not supported.

blind_target.authors: Kosloff, Spee; Irish, Spencer; Perreault, Leigh; Anderson, Gabrial; Nottbohm, Alexandra
blind_target.title: Assessing relationships between conformity and meta-traits in an Asch-like paradigm
blind_target.evidence_quote: We are particularly interested in the Big Five, intelligence, self-esteem, and the need for social approval.
blind_target.outcome_quote: Finally, we measured the Big Five, intelligence, self-esteem and social approval. With the exception of openness, our study finds no support that these personality traits are statistically significantly related to the susceptibility of group pressure.
blind_target.outcome_reasoning: Original neuroticism, agreeableness and conscientiousness associations are not supported, while openness, originally null, is associated here.

luna_triage.reason: The paper discusses Uchida et al.'s scholastic achievement proxy result, then explicitly frames its own analysis as directly measuring intelligence because prior studies used indirect school-grade measures. Its intelligence test does not retest the reported scholastic-achievement comparison.
luna_triage.location: Section 2.3 Individual differences (paragraph on intellectual competence)
luna_triage.omission_quote: Uchida et al. [ 31 ] studied 12 to 14 year-old high school students and assessed scholastic achievements by their school performance. They report that high achievers conformed less to the majority than low achievers.
luna_triage.identity_quote: Uchida   Akitoshi ,  Michael   Robert B. , and  Mori   Kazuo  ( 2020 ):  Scholastic achievement levels and conformity of junior high school students in the Asch experiment .  Psychology   11 :  1285 – 1299 .

luna_triage.reason: Kurosawa's cited effects concern the minority subject's decision following two confederates and the self-esteem of confederates in groups of four. The present H6 concerns the participant's self-esteem, so it does not retest either specified Kurosawa finding.
luna_triage.omission_quote: The effect of self-esteem (or self-assertiveness, self-consciousness) on conformity was only investigated in a few studies so far. Kurosawa [ 11 ] found no effect on conformity when the decision of the minority subject was preceded by two confederates. In groups of four, confederates’ self-esteem had a negative effect on conformity.

luna_triage.reason: The current paper predicts the same negative self-esteem–conformity association described for low-self-esteem witnesses, then tests participant self-esteem against conformity in its new sample. No supplied shipped original row represents Tainaka et al.

luna_triage.reason: Strickland and Crowne is described as confirming a positive association of social approval with conformity, and the current paper explicitly hypothesizes and measures that same association in its Asch line task. No supplied shipped original row represents this paper.

luna_triage.reason: The paper describes Kosloff et al.'s trait-specific Big Five findings and tests the Big Five in its Asch conformity task. This retests those personality-conformity associations in the new sample; no supplied shipped row represents Kosloff et al.
luna_triage.omission_quote: Kosloff et al. [ 19 ] found that subjects with low neuroticism, high agreeableness, and high conscientiousness scores show high levels of conformity. Extraversion, and openness were not associated with conformity ratings.
